newsitem.title: USA: Gun sales fall in California for third year.
newsitem.headline: Gun sales fall in California for third year.

text.p: Gun sales fell in California in 1996 for the third year in a row, state Attorney General Dan Lungren said on Friday.

Californians legally bought 353,872 guns and rifles during 1996, down 14 percent from 1995, when 411,668 were sold. That figure was down from 599,672 in 1994 and from a peak of 642,197 in 1993, Lungren's office said.

"In three years, we have gone from record high levels of gun sales to lows we haven't seen since the 1970s," said Lungren, a Republican. "What is most interesting is the rough correlation of declining gun sales with declining crime rates."

"Fewer people who believe they need guns to protect themselves mean more people believe our streets are safer. That is exactly what we in law enforcement are striving for, and I believe this shows that our community-oriented policing programmes and tougher laws are working," Lungren said.

In 1996, 3,642 people were barred from buying a gun under California's background check law which prevents guns from being legally sold to convicted felons, people with restraining orders against them or people with a history of mental health problems.

Among those barred from buying guns were 18 people with homicide convictions, four convicted kidnappers, 46 convicted sex offenders, 43 convicted robbers and 1,616 people with assault convictions, Lungren's office said.
Lungren also noted that, with more than 3 million guns bought in the state in the last six years, part of the downward trend in gun sales could be due to market saturation.
